blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's verified local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live listing feed or board statistics are attached to this page yet.

Dundarave is the District of West Vancouver's western village centre, built around the 2400 block of Marine Drive (24th and 25th Streets), with Dundarave Park and the pier at the foot of 25th Street. In the District's OCP it is one of West Vancouver's village centres, alongside the Ambleside Municipal Town Centre, the Park Royal regional shopping centre, and the village centres of Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay. Nearby areas: Ambleside (east), Altamont (west), the British Properties (north, uphill) and Chartwell (northeast).
This guide covers Dundarave's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Condo buildings in Dundarave
Dundarave is in the District of West Vancouver.
Seastrand — 150 24th Street (at Bellevue Avenue, village west edge)

A 16-storey concrete freehold-strata high-rise built in 1963 with 112 units (building directory). The directory records its strata restrictions as: pets allowed with restrictions, rentals allowed; amenities: elevator, guest suite, outdoor pool, shared laundry. Listings describe it as one of only two buildings in West Vancouver on the waterfront side of the train tracks. No source checked states any age restriction — general-market.

A 16-storey luxury concrete building by Cressey Development Group, completed 2020 (presale source), comprising 32 luxury condos and 3 townhomes per the presale source; developer material at groundbreaking described 35 private residences in total, which reconciles with 32 + 3. Published restrictions: listings record exercise centre, sauna/steam room, concierge and caretaker among amenities; pet, rental and age restrictions: Not confirmed from the sources opened — read the bylaws on the Form B. (55+ notes
Les Terraces — 2250 Bellevue Avenue

A boutique waterfront strata of only 11 private residences, one suite per floor (listing sources). Year built: listings conflict — one records 1990, another records 1991 — year built not confirmed between those two figures. A current listing records title as Freehold Strata, with indoor pool, elevator, concierge and caretaker among amenities, and pets "Yes With" (restrictions) in listing data. Age restriction: none stated in any source checked.
Rosemont — 2271 Bellevue Avenue

The building directory index records Rosemont at this address in Dundarave as freehold strata, 5 levels, completed 1994; a current listing confirms an Apartment/Condo unit in the building built in 1994, concrete/brick/stucco construction. Unit count: Not confirmed. Published pet/rental/age restrictions: Not confirmed from the sources opened.
Bellevue Gardens — 2119 Bellevue Avenue

A low-rise strata at the village's east edge: a current listing records an Apartment/Condo unit with strata fees, subdivision name "Bellevue Gardens," pets "Dogs OK" in listing data, and describes "a very proactive strata." Year built: the listing records 1978; a rental-directory page records 27 units, 4 storeys, built 1977 — year built not confirmed between 1977 and 1978, and the 27-unit count is single-source, so unit count is not confirmed. Age restriction: none stated in any source checked.
Regatta Pointe — 2280 Bellevue Avenue

A waterfront strata: a current listing names the building "Regatta Pointe," records the unit as Apartment/Condo built in 1989, with strata fees and pets "Yes With" (restrictions) in listing data, stepping directly onto the seawall. Unit count: Not confirmed. Age restriction: none stated in any source checked.

items.t: Dundarave is the District of West Vancouver's western village centre, built around the 2400 block of Marine Drive (24th and 25th Streets), with Dundarave Park and the pier at the foot of 25th Street. In the District's OCP it is one of West Vancouver's village centres, alongside the Ambleside Municipal Town Centre, the Park Royal regional shopping centre, and the village centres of Caulfeild Village and Horseshoe Bay. Nearby areas: Ambleside (east), Altamont (west), the British Properties (north, uphill) and Chartwell (northeast).

Where condo stock concentrates: on the waterfront shelf between Marine Drive and the seawalk, along Bellevue Avenue from 21st to 25th Streets and at the foot of 24th Street. Attached stock overall is modest: the balance of Dundarave is freehold detached homes on the slope north of Marine Drive, with waterfront and near-waterfront homes along Bellevue Avenue forming the premium tier.

Waterfront and park: Dundarave Park (150 25th Street) offers more than 50 metres of sandy beach, a playground, washrooms and a seasonal concession; the Centennial Seawalk runs about 1.7 km east from the park toward Ambleside.
Confirm catchments by exact address with West Vancouver Schools.

Transit: the Dundarave exchange at Marine Drive and 25th Street is served by the 250 Horseshoe Bay/Dundarave/Vancouver and 250A Dundarave/Vancouver on the Frequent Transit Network, the 255 Dundarave–Capilano University, the 251/252 locals to Park Royal, and the 253 (Caulfeild). The Blue Bus system is owned and operated by the District of West Vancouver under contract to TransLink.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Dundarave

items.t: District plans and zoning (West Vancouver's own bylaws only): Zoning Bylaw No. 4662, 2010 is the District's zoning bylaw — it specifies how land can be used and regulates intensity, height, density, setbacks and lot coverage. The Official Community Plan is OCP Bylaw No. 4985, 2018 (Council adopted Amendment Bylaw No. 5406, 2025 on December 1, 2025, aligning the OCP with the 2024 Interim Housing Needs Report). Dundarave Village Neighbourhood Centre is a named Form & Character Development Permit area, so new development, additions and renovations in the village core are reviewed against OCP design guidelines; a Foreshore Development Permit applies to waterfront properties and others at risk of coastal flooding, and an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank.

West Vancouver property taxes: for 2026, due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2 and a further 5% on September 2, 2026; roughly half the bill is collected for other taxing authorities, and water/sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly. At Dundarave price points the Province's additional school tax also applies: 0.2% on the residential portion assessed between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

Secondary suites (West Vancouver): the District permits secondary suites under Zoning Bylaw No. 4662 with its own registration process — one per lot, within the principal building (not detached), with the registered owner occupying either the principal dwelling or the suite. (55+ notes

blocks.text: Good to know about Dundarave

items.t: The village's most famous "condo" cannot be bought — and its replacement is not a presale. Villa Maris has been a single-owner rental building for 50 years; the redevelopment concept reported for it and the Shoreland has not even been submitted to the District, proposes rental first (206 units at the Shoreland site), and leaves the Pink Palace's strata replacement at an undecided size. Anyone marketing future Pink Palace condos today is ahead of the record.

The seawalk is the flat route between the two villages. The Centennial Seawalk runs about 1.7 km east from Dundarave Park to Ambleside — the level, paved waterfront route that connects Dundarave on foot to the Ambleside amenities, library and seniors centre corridor, and the reason the Bellevue shelf buildings trade on walkability rather than on the village strip alone.

Village-core changes are design-reviewed, not just permit-checked. The Dundarave Village Neighbourhood Centre is a named Form & Character Development Permit area in the OCP, so exterior work in the core is reviewed against design guidelines — including for the low-rise strata buildings a buyer might plan to renovate.

The "Dundarave" retirement supply is actually at 22nd Street. Westerleigh PARC's own marketing places it "on the edge of the Dundarave neighborhood" — a few blocks east of the 24th–25th Street village, next to the West Vancouver Community Centre and Seniors' Activity Centre corridor. Buyers searching "Dundarave retirement" are usually being shown this rental building.

The newest tower answers to two addresses in public sources. The Bellevue by Cressey appears as 2299 Bellevue Avenue in the area research and as 2289 Bellevue Avenue in current listings and its presale source — settle the civic address from the strata plan before a title search, a locator run or showing directions rely on either figure.

The Blue Bus is municipal. West Vancouver's bus system is owned and operated by the District of West Vancouver under contract to TransLink — it is not a TransLink-operated service, which is why Dundarave's Marine Drive service has its own local character.
There are no SnapStats numbers for West Vancouver.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Dundarave

items.t: Form B diligence (the counted strata component): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. For one of only three townhomes in a 35-home project, the Form B and depreciation report are where a buyer learns how tower-scale costs (elevator, envelope, amenity building) are shared with the townhome lots — read them before the view.

blocks.text: Good to know about Dundarave

items.t: A zoning section settles a marketing argument. "Village Point townhomes" survives in old ads and portal copy, but Bylaw 4662's CD2 zone was written for that one site (2388 Marine Drive) and permits apartments only, capped at 15 units — the same 15 the ads counted. When marketing and the bylaw disagree about built form in West Vancouver, the site-specific zone is the document to pull first.
Dundarave's only presale spent 2026 in receivership.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Dundarave
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots — the default and effectively the only land form: freehold detached dominates; a fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees. No bare-land strata development offered as vacant lots is verified for this ground.

Lot character: lots step up the slope north of Marine Drive; the flattest lots are the lower avenues between Marine Drive and Bellevue Avenue; Bellevue Avenue waterfront and near-waterfront lots are the premium tier. Typical lot dimensions and any average lot size: Not verified from an official source — the research's sub-area housing-mix breakdown (unit counts by type, average lot size, age of stock) is expressly not verified, so no figure is carried.
: None of it is lot inventory.

Dundarave Village Point (2388 Marine Drive) — apartment-form, counted NOWHERE as townhomes and not land: fresh verification in the townhomes pass documents it as apartment form — its own zoning, CD2 in Zoning Bylaw 4662, permits "apartments" to a maximum of 15 units, which governs over its 2010 "one level townhomes" marketing.
Pierwell (2468/2490 Marine Drive) — stalled/receivership presale, counted nowhere

TENURE TRAP — Villa Maris, the "Pink Palace" (2222 Bellevue Avenue): purpose-built single-owner RENTAL: per the District of West Vancouver's own 2024 Statement of Heritage Value — never strata and never land stock, whatever its condominium appearance suggests.

Assemblies/proposals, documented AS SUCH: the only density-change position documented for this ground is provincial, not a lot assembly — on July 21, 2025 the Province directed West Vancouver to amend its OCP to provide increased density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Ambleside and Dundarave (and at Park Royal–Taylor Way) by December 31, 2025.

items.t: Board position: "Dundarave" is the MLS sub-area name as the board (Greater Vancouver REALTORS) uses it. Nearby areas: Ambleside (east), Altamont (west), the British Properties (north, uphill) and Chartwell (northeast). Buyers also search "Dundarave Village," "West Van waterfront," and street searches around Bellevue Avenue, Haywood Avenue and 24th–29th Streets.

The SnapStats GVR September 2026 report contains no West Vancouver section at all — its GVR communities are Burnaby, New Westminster, Coquitlam, Port Coquitlam, Port Moody, Pitt Meadows and Maple Ridge.

Land shape: predominantly single-detached homes on the slope north of Marine Drive, with the flattest, most walkable pocket on the lower avenues between Marine Drive and Bellevue Avenue by the beach; waterfront and near-waterfront homes along Bellevue Avenue form the premium tier, with view homes stepping up the slope behind the village.

Waterfront: Dundarave Park (150 25th Street) offers more than 50 metres of sandy beach, a playground, washrooms and a seasonal concession, and it is where the Centennial Seawalk begins, running about 1.7 km east along the shore to Ambleside.

Schools (SD45 West Vancouver, Ministry-listed names): Irwin Park Elementary (K–7, 2455 Haywood Avenue) is in Dundarave itself; the catchment secondary school is West Vancouver Secondary (Grades 8–12, 1750 Mathers Avenue).

Culture: the West Vancouver Memorial Library (1950 Marine Drive, at 20th Street) is a few blocks east of the village; the West Vancouver Community Centre and Aquatic Centre in Ambleside is the indoor swimming and fitness facility.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Dundarave

items.t: OCP — District of West Vancouver Official Community Plan Bylaw 4985 (2018), which treats Dundarave as one of the District's village centres.
Zoning — District of West Vancouver Zoning Bylaw 4662 (2010): — West Vancouver's number only. Any parcel's actual zone: per-parcel, not verified here.

Form & Character: the Dundarave Village Neighbourhood Centre is a named Form & Character Development Permit area, so new development, additions and renovations in the village core are reviewed against OCP design guidelines — exterior changes near the core are not a simple building permit.

Hazard development-permit areas (as the research documents them): District-wide, an Environmental Development Permit is required for work within 15 metres of the top of a watercourse bank; a Wildfire Hazard DP applies within 100 metres of an undisturbed forest interface; and a Foreshore DP applies to waterfront properties and others at risk of coastal flooding — Bellevue Avenue waterfront lots should assume the Foreshore DP is in play from day one.

SSMUH / density transition — as the District/Province position stands: the Province's July 21, 2025 directive required increased density in the single-family and duplex areas adjacent to Dundarave by December 31, 2025; the District's final adopted zoning amendments for those areas were still outstanding as of November 2026 (the neighbouring Ambleside Centre Local Area Plan was implemented by provincial order effective April 7, 2026 — an Ambleside position, not a Dundarave one). Verify the current infill zoning per property before marketing multiplex potential.

Subdivision and servicing — District of West Vancouver servicing bylaw number not confirmed (held, never borrowed): The City of North Vancouver's numbers govern the City only and are NOT District of West Vancouver numbers. (Standing verified ledger, applied by exclusion.)

Property taxes — District of West Vancouver (a municipality; follow its own research): the 2026 payment was due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on unpaid current taxes on July 2 and a further 5% on September 2, 2026; roughly half the bill is collected for other taxing authorities, and water/sewer utilities are metered and billed quarterly. At Dundarave price points the Province's additional school tax also applies: 0.2% on the residential portion assessed between $3 million and $4 million and 0.4% above $4 million for 2026, rising to 0.3% and 0.6% on January 1, 2027.

ALR block (applies only where a parcel is ALR — none documented inside Dundarave, status per-parcel): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

blocks.text: Good to know about Dundarave

items.t: The seawalk starts here (Nov 1, 2026). The Centennial Seawalk begins at Dundarave Park and runs about 1.7 km east to Ambleside — one of the flattest waterfront walks on the North Shore, and the park itself holds more than 50 metres of sandy beach at 150 25th Street.

The buses are the District's own (Nov 1, 2026). The Blue Bus system serving Dundarave is owned and operated by the District of West Vancouver under contract to TransLink — a municipal operation, not a TransLink-owned fleet — and District OCP policy specifically supports better transit between Park Royal and Dundarave.
Village events could not be verified (Nov 1, 2026).

The density deadline passed without the local bylaw landing (Nov 1, 2026 research position). The Province's July 21, 2025 directive set a December 31, 2025 deadline for more density beside Dundarave, yet the research records the District's final adopted amendments as still outstanding as of November 2026 — while neighbouring Ambleside's plan was implemented by provincial order effective April 7, 2026. A lot's multiplex story here is therefore a per-property verification, not a headline.

Utilities are metered here (Nov 1, 2026). Unlike flat-fee municipalities, West Vancouver meters water/sewer and bills quarterly, on top of the July 2 tax due date — a carrying-cost detail land buyers comparing across the North Shore miss.
